title: AEGS AML/CFT Assessment
description:
The interface for an anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing finding. AEGS specifies **what must be recorded and what must be decidable**, not the detection method -- mandating one vendor's typology set would be beyond the competence of a technical standard and would freeze a fast-moving field.

IMPORTANT: emitting this object claims an assessment happened. An implementation without an AML control must omit it entirely rather than emit `score: 0`, which would assert a clean screening that never ran.

assessed.description: False means this control exists in the implementation and did not run for this action. Absent from a GovernanceDecision means the implementation does not have the control at all. The two are different statements and must not be collapsed.

score.description: Normalised 0..1, or null when genuinely unknown. Never 0 to mean 'unknown' -- an unmeasured value rendered as zero is not a missing fact, it is a wrong one, and no reader can tell the difference.

indicators.description: Named signals that fired. Absence of indicators is not evidence of absence of risk.

method.description: How the score was produced -- deterministic terms, a model, a third-party service. An auditor needs this to weigh the number.

typologies.description: Named patterns, e.g. structuring, layering, rapid movement, mule indicators.

reportable.description: Whether this action meets a reporting threshold. AEGS does not define thresholds -- they are jurisdictional.

provider.description: Third-party service, where used. Its output is evidence about the provider as much as the counterparty.
